outcome.technical: WHAT CHANGED (.github/workflows/ci.yml only; tools/verify.sh untouched): the `manifests + js + plugin` job is merged into the `lint` job, renamed `lint + manifests + e2e (linux)`, which now adds setup-node 20 and the npm ci + Claude CLI install step and runs `sh tools/verify.sh --only lint,runner,e2e,manifests,js,plugin`; its timeout goes 5 -> 6 and its `longest lint` line becomes an estimate of 2m38s (lint job's longest 1m50s in run 40774503871 + the manifests job's longest verify 38s, node 5s, install 5s over runs 40761628365..41070108164); the `longest manifests` line is removed; a comment above the job states the measured concurrency cap, its re-derive command, and that nothing checks the job count. WHY (measured, `gh run view <id> --json jobs`, read-only, seven release-tier runs over three days 2026-10-28..30: 40761628365 40765135807 40774503871 40877191420 40913965771 40946289828 41070108164): every run asked for 22 jobs and in every one exactly 2 started late, each 1-4 s after the 1st and 2nd job to finish - a cap of 20 concurrent jobs; in 6 of 7 runs a held job was a Windows sweep cell. In 41070108164 the held `windows, plain 4` started +95 s and set the wall (595 s) over the slowest cell (cp1252 4, 581 s). The per-run tier was 21 jobs (one held); merged it is 20. WHY NOT THE SPLIT: in 41070108164 the manifests job took 49 s (verify step 30 s) against a 581 s critical path, so a split cannot move the wall and adds jobs past the cap. It also cannot be made in my files: I built it in a scratch `git archive HEAD` copy (doctor/status-render/rendered-artifacts steps moved to a `doctor` slice in its own job): `python3 tools/gate-parity.py` exit 0, but `python3 tools/gate-parity.py --selftest` exit 1, 96/97, `FAIL sv14` - sv14 requires exactly one `--only ...manifests...` call holding every MANIFEST_WORK piece. The split needs tools/gate-parity.py (sv14), which is not my file; I stopped there. CHECKS RUN in the task worktree after the change: `python3 tools/gate-parity.py` exit 0 (13 slices, 7 jobs); `python3 tools/gate-parity.py --selftest` exit 0, ALL PASS 97/97; `gate-parity.py --list` shows manifests, js, plugin run by job `lint`; job_bound_evidence on the live text = [], and with timeout 5 it reports `lint ... under 2 times its longest recorded run of 2m38s (5m16s needed)`; `ruby -ryaml` loads the workflow (exit 0). The gate commands themselves were not run (runsGate own-tests, no tests of its own); browser gates not run as instructed. PREDICTION, per-run tier, from 41070108164's job times (resample excluded). WALL: no job held, so wall = slowest job = 581 s (9.7 min) on that run's balance, vs 595 s measured. On the committed table re-recorded from that run: 7978 slot-seconds total (sum of .github/sweep-costs.json `costs`) / 4 parts / 4 slots = 499 s of sweep per Windows cell at perfect packing, + 22 s job overhead (cp1252 4: 581 s job - 559 s verify step) = ~521 s = ~8.7 min. Over the 8 min (480 s) target. RUNNER-MINUTES: 106.3 - (49 + 91)/60 + (91 + 30 + 5 + 3)/60 = ~106.1 min. Over the 55 target: the 8 Windows sweep cells alone took 66.6 min (3998 s) in that run. NEITHER TARGET IS REACHABLE IN tools/verify.sh + ci.yml ALONE. Wall: Windows on 5 parts per leg = 7978/20 = 399 s + 22 = ~421 s (~7.0 min), with Linux legs on 2 parts each to stay at or under the cap (10 Windows + 4 Linux + e2e + lint + 2 browser = 18 jobs); browser (report), 429 s, would then be the critical path (~7.2 min). That needs tools/gate-parity.py (WINDOWS_SHARDS = 4 checked by sv13, sv15's literal fixture `shard: [1, 2, 3, 4]`, and shard_matrix_drift's every-part-on-every-runner rule for a per-family part count). Runner-minutes: with 39.5 min of non-Windows jobs (Linux sweep 23.0, browsers 12.6, e2e 1.7, merged lint ~2.2), 55 leaves 15.5 min for the Windows sweep, which takes 66.6 now. Getting there needs cuts to the Windows sweep's CPU (sweep-costs.json: test_drive_phase 2688.5, test_commit_task_work 665.4, test_audit_task 628.7, test_close_phase 470.4, test_stamp_verification 462.3 slot-s) or an owner decision to drop legs (Windows cp1252 34.8 min; dropping it AND Linux plain 11.4 still leaves ~60 min). The acceptance's five-run median is still unmeasured: every measured run is release-tier, and none is per-run. DEPENDANTS of tools/verify.sh (.gitattributes, ci.yml, derive-phase-gate.py, tests/test__output.py, tests/test__refs.py, tools/affected.py, tools/check-example-pins.py, tools/check-git-pipeline.py): still correct, because verify.sh is byte-unchanged (git status shows only ci.yml modified). DEPENDANTS of ci.yml: plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py, tests/test_audit_task.py, tests/test_drive_phase.py, tests/test__impact.py, tests/test__manifest_phases.py use the path as a fixture string or classification row and never read the real file, so they are still correct. tests/_harness.py names the selftest matrix's OSes in a docstring, and the matrix is unchanged, so it is still correct. tests/test__refs.py's real ci.yml use is a statement that every job is one verify.sh call, which is still true (each job's single run line is `sh tools/verify.sh --only ...`). tools/affected.py selects WORKFLOW_READERS on a ci.yml change: gate-parity (green above), sweep-selftests tt5 (selftests job bound 33 unchanged), check-rendered-artifacts ra29 (verify.sh call lines unchanged) and release.py rt2 (tier input unchanged). Not listed but affected by wording only: tools/gate-parity.py sv14's message says 'the manifest job's slice' (now the lint job; the predicate is unaffected); tests/test__doctor_policy.py's docstring calls CI's manifest job one that does not install the Claude CLI, which was already stale history before this change; tools/ci-verified.py fixtures use the old name 'lint + e2e (linux)' as fixture data only. main has no branch protection and no rulesets (`gh api .../branches/main/protection` 404 'Branch not protected', rulesets []), so the renamed check blocks no merge. Any CI-study parser outside this repo that reads the old lint or manifests job names would need updating.
outcome.descriptive: The manifests job is merged into the lint job so a per-run CI run fits GitHub's measured 20-concurrent-job cap and no Windows cell waits in the queue. The split was not made: it would add a job past the cap, and gate-parity sv14, a file outside this task, refuses it. Neither 8 min nor 55 runner-minutes can be reached by job shape alone.
